source_title: See-through pants problem causes Lululemon recall
publisher_issuer: CNN/Money (CNNMoney); figures corroborated by CBS News and SEC 8-K disclosures
company_context: Lululemon Athletica is a premium athletic-apparel retailer/DTC brand. In March 2013 it pulled certain black Luon women's yoga pants from shelves because they were too sheer, a quality_trust_failure for a premium brand whose value proposition rests on product quality. The recall affected a meaningful share of the women's pants assortment, hurt guidance, and was followed by leadership departures, but the company recovered over subsequent periods.
business_type: Premium athletic-apparel retail and direct-to-consumer (DTC), vertically branded
evidence_summary: In March 2013 Lululemon recalled certain black Luon women's yoga pants for excessive sheerness, affecting about 17% of all women's pants sold in its stores. The company guided to lost revenue of roughly $12-$17 million in the first quarter and $45-$50 million for the remainder of the year, and revised Q1 expectations from revenue of $350-$355 million (with ~11% comparable-store-sales growth) down to $333-$343 million (with ~5-8% growth). It recorded a $17.5 million inventory provision for the affected Luon during Q1 fiscal 2013. Leadership turnover followed: the Chief Product Officer left effective April 15, 2013, and CEO Christine Day announced on June 10, 2013 she would step down (with Laurent Potdevin succeeding her). The episode is a quality-trust failure with quantified near-term revenue and inventory impact followed by recovery.
outcome_evidence: Quantified lost-sales and inventory-provision impact and downward guidance revision in 2013, followed by leadership change; Lululemon subsequently recovered revenue growth in later periods, making this a quality-trust shock with recovery (temporary shock with recovery / quality failure).
source_limitations: Primary recorded source is named business journalism (CNNMoney) corroborated by CBS News and Lululemon 8-K disclosures on sec.gov; direct WebFetch of both CNN and sec.gov returned HTTP 403 in this environment, so figures rely on verbatim search-result snippets from those outlets/filings. Lost-revenue figures are company guidance ranges, not realized actuals. The exact realized full-year impact may differ from the guided ranges.

inferred: The damage was a product-quality/brand-trust failure, not a demand or pricing problem
